subject: se
question: What does multiplicity represent in a UML Class Diagram? Explain 1, 0..1, 1..* and 0..* with examples.
title: How Many Rules
hook: Every person has exactly one mother, but a mother can have zero, one or many children. UML writes those how-many rules as multiplicity.
answer: Multiplicity shows how many objects of one class can be linked to ONE object of the class at the other end of an association; it is written at the end of the association line.
1 = exactly one (a Book has exactly 1 Publisher).
0..1 = optional, at most one (a Student has 0..1 LibraryCard).
1..* = one or more, at least one (a Book has 1..* Authors).
0..* = zero or more, any number (a Student has 0..* IssueRecords).
Memory trick: the first number is the minimum, the second is the maximum.
